title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 41
paragraphs: At this time, being informed that the Phoenicians were at Tenedos, he filled five triremes with the property he had at hand and sailed away for Athens. Setting out from the city of Cardia, he was sailing through the Gulf of Melas; and as he passed along by the shore of the Chersonese, the Phoenicians fell in with his ships, and while Miltiades himself with four of his ships escaped to Imbros, the fifth ship was captured in the pursuit by the Phoenicians. In command of this ship, as it happened, was Metiochus, the eldest of Miltiades's sons—not born of the daughter of Olorus the Thracian, but of another woman. The Phoenicians captured him along with his ship; and being informed that he was the son of Miltiades, they brought him up to the king, thinking they would lay up for themselves a great obligation, because it was Miltiades who had declared his opinion to the Ionians that they should do as the Scythians said, at the time when the Scythians asked them to break up the bridge of boats and sail away to their own land. Darius, however, when the Phoenicians brought Metiochus son of Miltiades up to him, did Metiochus no harm, but on the contrary very much good: he gave him a house and possessions and a Persian wife, by whom he had children born who have been ranked as Persians. Miltiades meanwhile came from Imbros to Athens.
